identity.name: Calcium citrates
identity.chemical_class: calcium salts of citric acid (tricarboxylate salts)

function.mechanism: Buffers/adjusts food acidity and complexes metal ions; supplies calcium in formulation contexts.

adi.basis: Latest retrievable OpenEFSA re-evaluation record for E333 is ongoing and did not provide a published output/ADI in the API response.

efsa.key_finding: OpenEFSA question EFSA-Q-2011-00611 (E333 iii) is marked 'Ongoing Risk Assessment' (last modified 2026-01-19) with no published output object in the retrieved record.

concerns.summary: Recent clinical literature in nephrolithiasis contexts indicates calcium/citrate urinary balance is relevant to stone risk in susceptible groups; this is not direct proof of harm at typical additive exposure.
A prospective elderly cohort using oral calcium citrate reported mostly mild adverse reactions (mainly gastrointestinal) and no serious adverse reaction signal in that study context.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA entry for calcium citrate reports ADI NOT LIMITED (not specified).
21 CFR Part 184 (direct food substances affirmed as GRAS) includes 21 CFR 184.1195 calcium citrate with GMP-limited use conditions.
No specific IARC calcium citrate classification was identified in retrieved IARC search/classification pages.

adi_exceedance.notes: Numerical ADI exceedance assessment is not applicable for JECFA's 'not specified/not limited' ADI; EFSA numeric ADI was not retrievable from the latest ongoing record.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence remains permissive (FDA GRAS framework and JECFA ADI not specified/not limited). The latest retrievable EFSA E333 re-evaluation record is ongoing without a published output in the retrieved API result, and renal stone-risk literature supports caution for susceptible subgroups rather than broad population-level high concern.
key_factors: FDA listing in 21 CFR 184.1195 under Part 184 GRAS framework
OpenEFSA E333 re-evaluation currently marked ongoing with no retrieved output object
No major-jurisdiction ban identified in retrieved sources
Renal/lithogenic context evidence suggests subgroup caution at higher-risk physiology
